title: Energy Through a Food Web
question: Where does food energy go, and how much becomes new tissue at the next feeding level?

blocks.prompt: Required before tracing: If a consumer eats food, must all that food energy become its new tissue? Predict other destinations. Must the same percent reach every next feeding level? Explain.
blocks.text: I predict food energy can remain in feces or new tissue, and respiration eventually releases heat. Different feeding levels may transfer different percentages.

blocks.prompt: Required before tracing: Why compare production over the same area and period? How would you avoid counting the same transferred energy twice when following a branching food web?
blocks.text: Use production over the same1m²and model period. Follow each original input to distinct destinations; do not count transferred portions again as fresh energy.

blocks.prompt: Use your four feeding links to trace energy to the hawk along two paths. Why do the arrows point from food to eater? Why is this not a count of individual animals?
blocks.text: My web evidence: plant→grasshopper→hawk and plant→rabbit→hawk trace food chemical energy to eater, not numbers of animals. Chosen net plant production1000after plant respiration,300eaten by hopper and200rabbit. Hopper300−90unabsorbed−180respired=30new tissue; rabbit20and hawk5supplied. Hawk eats15hopper+10rabbit=25, with5unabsorbed+15respired+5new tissue. Level production50/1000×100=5%and5/50×100=10%, different from5/25×100=20%of food eaten by hawk. Final distinct destinations315eventual heat,155chemical energy in feces and530remaining new tissue(500plant+15hopper+10rabbit+5hawk)=1000. Not all untransferred energy is already heat; decomposers can later use detrital chemical energy, nutrients cycle but food energy is not recycled from heat. Summing1000+50+5double-counts transfers. blocks.prompt: What happens to the90kJ in the grasshopper’s unabsorbed food?
blocks.text:
It remains chemical energy in feces and can enter a detrital food path.
Correct! Unabsorbed food retains chemical energy. Respiration and eventual heat release are different destinations; energy is conserved. Revised after feedback.

blocks.prompt: What denominator measures producer-to-herbivore level transfer here?
blocks.text:
Producer net production1000kJ over the same area and period.
Correct! Level transfer compares higher-level new production with lower-level new production. Dividing by food actually eaten answers a different question.

blocks.prompt: Can1000+50+5be used as three separate energy inputs?
blocks.text:
No. Some of the same energy is transferred through these levels, so that sum double-counts it.
Correct! Consumer production comes from earlier food energy. Track the original input to distinct final destinations instead of summing repeated transfers.

Original drawings, food links and energy values are teaching assumptions, not photographs, empirical species diets or universal rates. Organism size and arrow width do not encode biomass, abundance or energy amount. Start with1000kJ of net plant production after plant respiration; sunlight input and plant respiration lie outside this budget. Only new production from this period is followed. Some remains uneaten in living tissue at the end; it is not all standing biomass. Unabsorbed food remains chemical energy in the detrital path, which includes waste and dead material. Later decomposition, death, other excretion and exports are not simulated. Decomposers can use detrital chemical energy and release heat; nutrients cycle, but heat is not recycled as food energy. Respired energy is not destroyed. The supplied transfer percentages are not constants for every ecosystem or a prediction of animal population size.
